meta.identity: expected impact = N x G x dC x E x A
meta.note: Opportunities are derived from the disease catalogue, the coverage and effectiveness parameters, and the cost anchors used elsewhere in this project. They are illustrative allocation objects for studying how people value different kinds of genetic-medicine impact — not solicitations, and not endorsements of any named programme. Impact in the two research markets is probability-weighted using explicit modelling assumptions.
caveats: Opportunities overlap. The same affected birth can be avoided by carrier screening, embryo selection or prenatal diagnosis, so impacts must not be added together — only the funding asks are additive.
Impact is assumed to scale linearly with the funded share of an opportunity.
Cost anchors for editing programmes remain provisional (see DATA_NEEDED.md).
Research success probabilities are assumptions, not forecasts.
The three markets are not denominated in the same units and should not be summed into a single impact number.

impact_now.label: Impact now
impact_now.question: Which projects most efficiently close known gaps between what genetic medicine can already do and who actually receives it?
impact_now.outcome_unit: affected births avoided or infants treated early, per year

translational.label: Translational R&D
translational.question: Which research would most raise the chance that a safe option exists for families who cannot select an unaffected embryo?
translational.outcome_unit: probability-weighted reproductive situations served per year
translational.best_cost_per_outcome_title: International registry and long-term follow-up infrastructure

future.label: Future research
future.question: Which research would most expand what heritable intervention could reach in common polygenic disease?
future.outcome_unit: probability-weighted common diseases brought within reach

opportunities.title: Prenatal diagnosis — Lower-middle income
opportunities.effectiveness_source: prenatal detection of major structural anomalies (CHD, NTD)
assumptions: One programme serves every catalogue condition the panel covers; impact is summed across 95 conditions rather than billed to one.
Coverage rises from the region's modelled current reach to the achievable-2035 standard for this tool.
Impact scales linearly with the funded share of the gap.

opportunities.incidence_source: GBD 2023 (Sickle cell disorders, <1yr birth incidence, Global)

Impact scales linearly with the funded share of the gap.

opportunities.title: Preclinical safety package for single-gene correction
opportunities.detail: Off-target, mosaicism and long-term-safety evidence sufficient to support a first tightly governed clinical protocol in catastrophic monogenic disease.
assumptions: Probability of technical success 55% and of translation to an approved option 35% — modelling assumptions, not forecasts.
The programme is relevant to 60% of the modelled no-selectable-embryo population.
Impact is future-dated and does not accrue within the funding period.

opportunities.title: Non-clinical embryo models for correction research
opportunities.detail: Model systems that let correction efficiency and off-target effects be measured without creating clinical embryos.
assumptions: Probability of technical success 70% and of translation to an approved option 30% — modelling assumptions, not forecasts.
The programme is relevant to 45% of the modelled no-selectable-embryo population.
Impact is future-dated and does not accrue within the funding period.

opportunities.title: Higher-fidelity editing chemistry and delivery
opportunities.detail: Editing approaches with high on-target conversion at the single-cell stage, the rate-limiting step for any heritable correction.
assumptions: Probability of technical success 50% and of translation to an approved option 40% — modelling assumptions, not forecasts.
The programme is relevant to 75% of the modelled no-selectable-embryo population.
Impact is future-dated and does not accrue within the funding period.

opportunities.title: International registry and long-term follow-up infrastructure
opportunities.detail: Shared outcome reporting for any approved heritable intervention — the precondition for evaluating whether early cases actually benefit.
assumptions: Probability of technical success 85% and of translation to an approved option 50% — modelling assumptions, not forecasts.
The programme is relevant to 30% of the modelled no-selectable-embryo population.
Impact is future-dated and does not accrue within the funding period.

opportunities.title: Causal-variant discovery for common disease
opportunities.detail: Moving from association to causation at scale — the binding constraint on any polygenic intervention.
opportunities.outcome_unit: modelled common diseases brought within reach, probability-weighted
assumptions: Probability of technical success 45% and of translation 25% — modelling assumptions, not forecasts.
Scale is anchored on the 3 of 10 modelled common diseases that meet the editing threshold under the near-future capacity scenario, which is an assumption set rather than a prediction.
Benefits, if any, arrive beyond the modelled horizon.
